domain_label: Knowledge Distillation & Dense Representation (Schema-Constrained Distillation & Dense-to-Human Rendering subdomain)
assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
subdomain scope is per-chunk distillation into dense JSON, constrained decoding, losslessness enforcement, and dense-to-human rendering
teacher model is accessible for soft label generation or CoT trace extraction
distillation targets specialist LLMs deployed in orchestrated multi-specialist systems
key references: Hinton/Vinyals/Dean 2015 (dark knowledge); Willard & Louf 2023 (Outlines constrained decoding)
exclusions: vector embedding generation and dense retrieval indexing
privacy and PII handling in distilled records

competency_questions.question: What theoretical basis justifies training a student model on teacher soft outputs rather than hard labels?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: KD_THEORY defines dark knowledge, temperature scaling, and soft-target benefit

competency_questions.question: How is the distillation loss designed and what temperature controls gradient informativeness?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DISTILL_OBJECTIVE defines KL divergence, temperature T, hard-label weight alpha, and feature matching options

competency_questions.question: How is each source chunk distilled into a dense JSON record and what schema governs the output?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CHUNK_DISTILL and JSON_SCHEMA_DESIGN define the distillation procedure and field taxonomy

competency_questions.question: How is guaranteed-valid JSON output achieved without post-hoc repair?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONSTRAINED_DECODING defines FSM-based grammar-constrained decoding via Outlines

competency_questions.question: How is schema evolved over time without breaking existing consumers or distilled record stores?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SCHEMA_VERSIONING defines version field, migration scripts, and backward compatibility rules

competency_questions.question: How are dense JSON records rendered into human-readable form for downstream consumers?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DENSE_RENDERER defines template engine, field-to-sentence mapping, and rendering fidelity check

competency_questions.question: How is losslessness of distillation measured and enforced across entity, numeric, and caveat retention?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LOSSLESSNESS_CHECK defines entity recall, numeric fact preservation, and caveat retention metrics

competency_questions.question: How is Goodhart's Law and benchmark contamination monitored to ensure metric gains reflect real utility?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GOODHART_MONITOR defines canary benchmarks, contamination scanning, and human eval correlation requirement

competency_questions.question: How is orchestration latency and cost modeled for a multi-specialist LLM routing system?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ORCH_LATENCY and GPU_COST_MODEL define latency compounding, SLA budgeting, and cost projection

competency_questions.question: How is routing logic implemented and what fallback mechanism handles out-of-scope queries?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ROUTING_LOGIC defines query classifier, confidence threshold, specialist dispatch, and generalist fallback

competency_questions.question: How are teacher model license/ToS constraints evaluated and enforced before distillation begins?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TEACHER_SELECTION defines license review, ToS compliance check, and open-weight fallback

competency_questions.question: When should CoT-trace distillation substitute for logit-level distillation and what additional risks does it introduce?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROMPT_DISTILL and CA_08 define the fallback condition, trace review requirement, and hallucination risk

glossary.definition: information encoded in teacher soft output probability distributions over all classes; inter-class similarity information absent from hard one-hot labels
division of logits by temperature T before softmax; high T produces softer distributions revealing more inter-class information
generation method that masks invalid tokens at each step using a finite-state machine compiled from a target grammar or JSON schema, guaranteeing structural validity of output
property of a distillation ensuring all semantically load-bearing facts in source are recoverable from the dense representation; measured by entity recall, numeric preservation, caveat retention
ratio of source token count to distilled JSON token count; higher ratio means denser representation
when a measure becomes a target it ceases to be a good measure; in LLM context: benchmark optimization without real utility improvement
distilled LLM trained on a narrow task domain that outperforms a generalist of comparable or larger size within that domain
metadata record linking each distilled JSON record to its source chunk, teacher model version, prompt template hash, schema version, and distillation timestamp
knowledge transfer via chain-of-thought reasoning traces extracted from teacher rather than logit distributions; used when teacher logits are inaccessible (API-only teacher)
process of compiling a JSON Schema or regex grammar into a finite-state machine over the model tokenizer vocabulary, used by Outlines for constrained decoding

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for knowledge distillation and dense representation engineering work units in absence of supplied datasets; grounded in Hinton/Vinyals/Dean 2015 and Willard/Louf 2023 as conceptual anchors

nodes.definition: Understand the theoretical basis of knowledge distillation (Hinton/Vinyals/Dean 2015): training a student model to match soft probability outputs (dark knowledge) of a teacher, enabling model compression with minimal accuracy loss.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new teacher architecture or distillation objective adopted

pros.claim: Soft targets carry inter-class similarity information absent in hard labels
pros.example: cat/dog logits share structure that trains student better than one-hot

cons.claim: Teacher quality ceiling: student cannot exceed teacher accuracy
cons.example: distilling a weak teacher yields a weak student regardless of effort

failure_modes: conflating soft-label distillation with response distillation only
ignoring temperature effect on gradient magnitude
acceptance_tests: student loss on soft targets lower than hard-label baseline on held-out set
temperature sweep documented with rationale for chosen T

nodes.definition: Distill each source text chunk into a maximally dense JSON representation retaining all semantically load-bearing information: entities, relations, numeric facts, caveats, provenance, and structure — while eliminating redundancy and filler.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: schema version bump or new chunk type added to pipeline

pros.claim: Schema-constrained output enforces completeness and parseability
pros.example: structured fields prevent omitting numeric facts that prose summaries drop

cons.claim: Schema over-specification silences emergent facts not fitting predefined fields
cons.example: novel entity types discarded if schema has no slot for them

failure_modes: omitting numeric quantities or dates
conflating chunk boundary with semantic boundary
losing caveats and negations
acceptance_tests: round-trip fidelity check: all named entities in source appear in JSON
no placeholder or null fields where source provides values
schema validation passes on 100% of chunks
revisit_triggers: new entity types observed in corpus

nodes.definition: Design the JSON schema that governs dense chunk records: field taxonomy, required vs optional fields, type constraints, nested object structure, and forward-compatibility versioning strategy.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: domain ontology revision or new field type required

pros.claim: Explicit schema enables automated validation and catches regressions immediately
pros.example: CI schema lint catches missing required field before it reaches production

cons.claim: Rigid schema accumulates technical debt as domain evolves
cons.example: adding new entity type requires breaking schema change and migration

failure_modes: under-specifying required fields allowing nulls to pass
coupling schema to one LLM's output idioms
acceptance_tests: schema passes JSON Schema 2020-12 validator
sample of 50 distilled records fully validates against schema
schema includes version field and migration notes
revisit_triggers: new entity type encountered in data

nodes.definition: Apply structured/grammar-constrained decoding (e.g., Outlines — Willard & Louf 2023) to guarantee LLM outputs are valid JSON conforming to a target schema, eliminating post-hoc repair and parse failures.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new Outlines/lm-format-enforcer version or schema structural change

pros.claim: Eliminates entire class of parse failures by construction
pros.example: no try/except JSON repair needed; outputs always valid

cons.claim: FSM compilation overhead adds latency; large schemas compile slowly
cons.example: complex recursive schemas can produce FSMs with 10^6+ states

failure_modes: schema with recursive references causing FSM explosion
tokenizer mismatch between schema compiler and inference runtime
acceptance_tests: parse failure rate = 0% on 1000-record sample
FSM compilation completes in under 30s for target schema
output satisfies JSON Schema validation on all test inputs

nodes.definition: Measure and enforce losslessness of distillation by comparing source chunk content to distilled JSON: detect dropped facts, altered numerics, missing caveats, and entity omissions via automated round-trip fidelity checks.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: fidelity metric falls below threshold on new corpus sample

pros.claim: Automated fidelity catch prevents silent information loss at scale
pros.example: NLI entailment check catches dropped negations that human review misses

cons.claim: NLI-based entailment checks have false positives on paraphrastic content
cons.example: paraphrase of numeric fact may fail entailment check incorrectly

failure_modes: treating summarization metrics (ROUGE) as fidelity proxies
missing negation/caveat extraction
acceptance_tests: entity recall >= 0.95 on test set
numeric fact preservation rate >= 0.99
caveat/negation retention rate >= 0.90

nodes.definition: Build a decompression/rendering model that reconstructs human-readable prose or structured reports from dense JSON KB records, enabling downstream consumers to read distilled knowledge without raw JSON exposure.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: schema version bump or new consumer format requirement

pros.claim: Decouples consumer interface from internal representation enabling schema evolution
pros.example: schema v2 JSON renders identically to consumer via template update only

cons.claim: Template-based rendering cannot capture emergent relational nuance in nested JSON
cons.example: complex multi-hop relations flatten poorly into prose sentences

failure_modes: template drift from schema (missing new fields in render)
over-templating producing robotic unreadable output
acceptance_tests: rendered output passes human readability review on 20-record sample
all required schema fields appear in rendered output
rendering roundtrip: parse rendered prose back to JSON recovers >= 90% of fields

nodes.definition: Select the teacher model for distillation considering capability ceiling, license/ToS compliance (API distillation restrictions), compute cost, and alignment with the target student domain.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: model ToS change or new open-weight release in domain

pros.claim: License-aware selection prevents downstream legal and deployment blocks
pros.example: OpenAI ToS prohibits using API outputs to train competing models; must use open-weight teacher for that use case

cons.claim: Best available teacher may be legally off-limits forcing capability compromise
cons.example: frontier API model outperforms open-weight alternative but is restricted

failure_modes: using API-accessed model outputs for student training without checking ToS
selecting teacher without domain overlap with student target task
acceptance_tests: license/ToS review completed and documented before any distillation run
teacher domain benchmark score exceeds student baseline by >= 10 points
revisit_triggers: new open-weight model releases potentially dominating

nodes.definition: Choose student model architecture and size balancing inference latency, serving cost, target accuracy after distillation, and specialist-beats-generalist narrowness constraints.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new architecture family releases or serving latency budget revision

pros.claim: Specialist student at 1/10 teacher size can match teacher on narrow task
pros.example: 7B coding specialist matches 70B generalist on HumanEval

cons.claim: Student too small for task complexity fails to absorb teacher dark knowledge
cons.example: <1B student cannot absorb reasoning chains from 70B teacher on multi-step tasks

failure_modes: choosing architecture without measuring target task complexity
ignoring inference latency constraints during selection
acceptance_tests: student latency meets serving SLA in benchmark
student accuracy post-distillation within 5% of teacher on target task
revisit_triggers: target task scope expands beyond specialist boundary

nodes.definition: Design the combined distillation loss: soft-target KL divergence at temperature T, optional hard-label cross-entropy, intermediate layer matching (feature distillation), and task-specific auxiliary losses.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: teacher architecture change or new auxiliary task introduced

pros.claim: Temperature scaling of soft targets controls gradient informativeness optimally for each task
pros.example: T=4 for classification tasks; T=8 for generation tasks empirically robust

cons.claim: Feature distillation adds complexity with architecture-dependent layer alignment cost
cons.example: layer-matching breaks when teacher/student depth ratio is non-integer

failure_modes: setting alpha=1.0 (hard labels only) negating soft-target benefit
mismatched temperature between teacher inference and student training
acceptance_tests: ablation shows soft-target loss component improves over hard-label-only baseline
temperature T chosen with sweep over {1,2,4,8,16} on validation set
revisit_triggers: teacher architecture change breaks feature alignment

nodes.definition: Build the data pipeline generating teacher soft labels on the training corpus: batched teacher inference, soft label storage (logit caching), curriculum ordering, and data quality filtering.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: teacher model checkpoint update or corpus distribution change

pros.claim: Caching teacher logits amortizes teacher inference cost across multiple student training runs
pros.example: pre-cached labels enable 10x faster student training iteration

cons.claim: Cached labels go stale if teacher model updated mid-experiment
cons.example: v1 teacher labels mixed with v2 teacher labels corrupts training signal

failure_modes: mixing teacher versions in cached labels
skipping deduplication leading to memorization of repeated examples
acceptance_tests: label cache versioned and tied to teacher model checkpoint hash
deduplication pass confirms < 0.1% duplicate examples in training split

nodes.definition: Evaluate distilled student on target-task benchmarks and monitor for Goodhart/contamination: benchmark gaming, training-set leakage, and metric divergence from real user value.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: benchmark contamination detected or human eval diverges from benchmark

pros.claim: Multi-benchmark evaluation reduces Goodhart risk vs single-metric optimization
pros.example: HumanEval + MBPP + custom internal test; gaming one does not game all

cons.claim: Benchmark contamination in pretraining data inflates reported student scores
cons.example: model may have seen benchmark examples during pretraining corpus

failure_modes: reporting only peak benchmark without held-out validation
ignoring human eval when benchmark diverges from user satisfaction
acceptance_tests: contamination scan run before reporting any benchmark number
held-out human eval conducted on >= 100 examples per task
benchmark and human eval scores agree within 8 percentage points
revisit_triggers: production user satisfaction metrics diverge from benchmark

nodes.definition: Model and bound the latency and cost of orchestrating multiple specialist distilled LLMs: routing overhead, sequential vs parallel call patterns, token cost compounding, and SLA budgeting.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: SLA revision or new specialist model added to routing topology

pros.claim: Parallel specialist calls can hide serial chain latency under a single SLA budget
pros.example: two specialists called in parallel adds only max(latency_A, latency_B) not sum

cons.claim: Each orchestration hop adds network + queue latency that compounds non-linearly
cons.example: 4-specialist chain adds 4x network overhead on top of inference latency

failure_modes: ignoring cold-start latency in SLA projections
summing latencies for parallel calls instead of taking max
acceptance_tests: end-to-end latency p95 within SLA budget on load test
cost-per-query projection within approved budget at target QPS
revisit_triggers: new specialist added to routing graph

nodes.definition: Define the narrow task scope within which a specialist distilled LLM reliably outperforms a generalist: boundary conditions, out-of-scope detection, fallback routing, and scope drift monitoring.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: production query distribution shift or new task type emerges

pros.claim: Explicit scope boundary prevents silent degradation when queries drift outside specialist domain
pros.example: out-of-scope detector routes medical queries away from legal specialist

cons.claim: Scope boundary is fuzzy; edge cases degrade gracefully or catastrophically with no clean threshold
cons.example: legal-medical boundary queries handled poorly by both specialists

failure_modes: deploying specialist on out-of-scope traffic without fallback
defining scope too narrowly causing excessive fallback overhead
acceptance_tests: specialist outperforms generalist by >= 10 points within defined scope on benchmark
out-of-scope detector precision >= 0.90 on boundary test set
revisit_triggers: new task type added to product

nodes.definition: Distill teacher reasoning traces and chain-of-thought into compact instruction-following demonstrations for student fine-tuning, enabling reasoning transfer without full logit distillation.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: teacher reasoning style change or new multi-step task added

pros.claim: CoT distillation enables reasoning transfer when teacher API does not expose logits
pros.example: when using GPT-4 API (logits unavailable) CoT traces substitute for soft targets

cons.claim: Compressed CoT traces may introduce reasoning shortcuts or hallucinated steps
cons.example: teacher CoT may include confident-sounding incorrect reasoning steps

failure_modes: distilling hallucinated CoT steps as ground truth
compressing reasoning traces so heavily structure is lost
acceptance_tests: human review of 50 sampled CoT traces for correctness before training
student reasoning accuracy on trace-verified test set >= teacher accuracy - 5%
revisit_triggers: teacher model updated with different reasoning style
task requires multi-step reasoning beyond trace length

nodes.definition: Set and measure the target compression ratio between source content token count and distilled JSON token count, balancing density against losslessness constraints.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: schema expansion or losslessness threshold revision

pros.claim: Token-efficiency target enforces discipline preventing verbose JSON that defeats compression purpose
pros.example: without target engineers add redundant fields until JSON is longer than source

cons.claim: Aggressive compression targets incentivize dropping low-frequency but high-value facts
cons.example: rare numeric outliers dropped to meet compression target

failure_modes: setting compression target without losslessness floor
measuring compression on token count without measuring information retention
acceptance_tests: compression ratio >= 3:1 on test corpus while maintaining entity recall >= 0.95
tradeoff curve plotted and reviewed before production target set
revisit_triggers: new field types added to schema increase token count

nodes.definition: Implement schema version control for distilled JSON records: version field, backward-compatible evolution rules, migration scripts, and deprecation policy for old schema versions.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: major schema restructuring or new consumer integration

pros.claim: Version field enables consumers to handle multiple schema generations without breaking
pros.example: renderer handles v1 and v2 records simultaneously during migration window

cons.claim: Backward compatibility constraints limit schema optimization opportunities
cons.example: cannot rename field without breaking v1 consumers even when name is misleading

failure_modes: breaking schema changes without version bump
no migration path for legacy records in existing storage
acceptance_tests: all schema changes increment version field
migration script tested on 1000 production records before deployment
rollback to prior schema version tested and documented

nodes.definition: Implement the orchestration routing layer that classifies incoming queries and dispatches to the appropriate specialist LLM, including confidence thresholding, multi-specialist ensemble, and fallback to generalist.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new specialist added to registry or query distribution shifts

pros.claim: Confidence-thresholded routing prevents specialist misapplication on ambiguous queries
pros.example: threshold=0.85 on router classifier reduces out-of-scope specialist calls by 60%

cons.claim: Router itself is an ML model with its own error rate compounding specialist errors
cons.example: router misclassification + specialist error = compounded failure invisible to user

failure_modes: routing without confidence threshold allowing low-confidence specialist dispatch
no audit log making routing failures invisible
acceptance_tests: routing audit log captures every dispatch decision with confidence score
fallback rate < 15% on production traffic sample
end-to-end accuracy with routing >= specialist accuracy on in-scope test set

nodes.definition: Continuously monitor for Goodhart's Law manifestations and benchmark contamination: detect when metric improvement does not correspond to real task utility improvement, and scan training data for benchmark leakage.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: training corpus update or new public benchmark released

pros.claim: Canary test sets not in training distribution catch Goodhart gaming reliably
pros.example: private canary benchmark maintained internally reveals when public benchmark games

cons.claim: Contamination scanning is incomplete; embedding similarity misses paraphrase contamination
cons.example: benchmark rephrased in training data evades n-gram contamination scan

failure_modes: relying solely on public benchmarks without human eval correlation
no canary test sets maintained independently of public benchmarks
acceptance_tests: contamination scan run on training corpus before benchmark reporting
human eval correlation with benchmark score >= 0.75 (Pearson)
private canary benchmark maintained and score not shared publicly
revisit_triggers: new benchmark added to evaluation suite

nodes.definition: Implement and run the student fine-tuning training loop on distillation data: optimizer config, learning rate schedule, gradient clipping, checkpoint selection, and early stopping on validation distillation loss.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: distillation dataset update or student architecture revision

pros.claim: Validation-loss-based early stopping prevents overfitting to teacher noise
pros.example: training beyond valley of val loss adds teacher hallucination artifacts to student

cons.claim: Learning rate schedule sensitivity high; wrong schedule dominates other hyperparameter effects
cons.example: cosine vs linear decay can differ by 3 benchmark points on same data

failure_modes: training without validation split causing overfit to full distillation set
no gradient clipping causing loss spikes on hard examples
acceptance_tests: validation loss curve shows convergence before checkpoint selection
gradient norm logged and clipping triggered < 5% of steps
checkpoint selected by validation loss not training loss

nodes.definition: Model GPU/compute cost of the full distillation pipeline: teacher inference (label generation), student training, hyperparameter sweep, and re-distillation cycles; set budgets and detect cost overruns early.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: GPU pricing change or re-distillation cycle triggered

pros.claim: Early cost modeling prevents budget overruns that kill projects mid-training
pros.example: teacher label generation at $0.01/1k tokens on 100M token corpus = $1000; model early

cons.claim: Cost models go stale quickly as GPU spot prices and model efficiency change
cons.example: spot price volatility makes 30-day cost projections unreliable

failure_modes: starting large teacher inference run without cost estimate
not accounting for re-distillation cost after teacher model update
acceptance_tests: cost estimate reviewed and approved before any teacher inference run > 1k GPU-hours
budget alert fires when actual spend exceeds 80% of projected cost
revisit_triggers: teacher model update requiring re-generation of labels

nodes.definition: Track full provenance of distilled records: source chunk identifier, teacher model version, distillation prompt hash, schema version, distillation timestamp, and human review status.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: teacher model update or prompt template revision

pros.claim: Provenance enables targeted re-distillation when teacher or prompt changes
pros.example: only re-distill records from teacher v1 without regenerating all v2 records

cons.claim: Provenance storage overhead grows linearly with corpus size and re-distillation count
cons.example: 10 re-distillation cycles on 1M chunks = 10M provenance records

failure_modes: losing teacher version association making targeted re-distillation impossible
no prompt hash meaning prompt changes are invisible in audit trail
acceptance_tests: every distilled record has non-null teacher_model_hash and prompt_template_hash fields
lineage graph query returns full re-distillation history for any chunk id

nodes.definition: Define and operate the human review gate for distilled JSON records: sampling strategy, review criteria, reviewer calibration, disagreement resolution, and escalation for high-risk record types.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new high-risk record type or reviewer pool change

pros.claim: Human review catches systematic distillation errors that automated checks miss
pros.example: numeric sign errors in distilled records not caught by schema validation

cons.claim: Human review is expensive and creates throughput bottleneck at scale
cons.example: 100% human review of 1M records is infeasible; sampling required

failure_modes: reviewing only easy cases (high losslessness score) missing systematic hard-case errors
no reviewer calibration leading to inconsistent acceptance criteria
acceptance_tests: reviewer inter-annotator agreement >= 0.80 (Cohen kappa) on calibration set
high-risk record type (numeric-heavy, medical, legal) review rate >= 20%
escalation path documented and tested

edges.resolution_rule: cost_budget_cap_gates_pipeline_scale; reduce corpus size or switch to cheaper teacher if budget exceeded
losslessness_floor_dominates_compression_target; reduce compression ratio until losslessness threshold met
human_eval_correlation_dominates_benchmark_score; if divergence detected prioritize human eval over benchmark optimization

conflict_axes.pole_a: maximize losslessness: retain every fact, entity, caveat, and numeric value
conflict_axes.pole_b: maximize token compression: minimize JSON token count for storage/inference efficiency
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: set losslessness floor first (entity recall >= 0.95), then compress within that constraint

conflict_axes.pole_a: strict schema: every field typed, required fields enforced, no extras allowed
conflict_axes.pole_b: flexible schema: open additionalProperties to capture emergent content
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use strict schema with a versioned catch-all field for emergent content

conflict_axes.pole_a: use frontier API teacher for maximum distillation quality
conflict_axes.pole_b: use open-weight teacher to comply with ToS and avoid API distillation restrictions
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: license compliance is non-negotiable; select best open-weight teacher within legal constraints

conflict_axes.pole_a: maximize specialist accuracy by routing all queries to best specialist
conflict_axes.pole_b: minimize orchestration cost by reducing specialist calls and routing hops
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: model full cost including routing latency; parallelize where possible

conflict_axes.pole_a: optimize reported benchmark scores for product credibility
conflict_axes.pole_b: optimize real user utility as measured by human eval and production metrics
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: maintain private canary benchmarks and enforce human eval correlation check before promotion

conflict_axes.pole_a: minimize student size for serving cost and latency
conflict_axes.pole_b: maximize student capacity to absorb teacher knowledge and hit accuracy targets
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: set minimum accuracy floor on target task; find smallest student that meets it

conflict_axes.pole_a: fully automated distillation pipeline for throughput and cost efficiency
conflict_axes.pole_b: extensive human review gates for accuracy and safety on high-risk record types
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: risk-stratify records; automate low-risk, human-review high-risk types

conflict_axes.pole_a: full logit-level KL distillation for maximal knowledge transfer fidelity
conflict_axes.pole_b: CoT trace distillation when teacher logits unavailable (API-only teacher)
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: prefer logit distillation when teacher accessible; use CoT distillation as fallback with human trace review

conflict_axes.pole_a: evolve schema aggressively to optimize representation as domain understanding matures
conflict_axes.pole_b: maintain strict backward compatibility to avoid breaking consumers and migration costs
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: version all schema changes; maintain compatibility matrix; deprecate with migration window

conflict_axes.pole_a: minimize GPU spend by limiting teacher inference, HPO sweeps, and re-distillation
conflict_axes.pole_b: maximize distillation quality by running large teacher inference and extensive HPO
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: cost-gate teacher inference runs; limit HPO to high-impact hyperparameters identified by prior ablation

edge_cases.title: teacher_api_tos_change_mid_project
edge_cases.description: Teacher API ToS updated to prohibit distillation after label generation has begun; cached labels may be legally contaminated.
edge_cases.trigger: ToS change notification received after partial label caching
edge_cases.recommended_action: halt pipeline; legal review; switch to open-weight teacher; discard contaminated labels

edge_cases.title: constrained_decoding_fsm_explosion
edge_cases.description: Recursive or deeply nested schema causes FSM state explosion during Outlines compilation, making constrained decoding infeasible.
edge_cases.trigger: FSM compilation time > 5 minutes or memory OOM during schema compilation
edge_cases.recommended_action: refactor schema to remove recursion; use partial schema constraint for top-level fields only

edge_cases.title: losslessness_below_threshold_on_new_chunk_type
edge_cases.description: New chunk type (e.g., tabular data, mathematical equations) causes entity recall to drop below 0.95 losslessness floor.
edge_cases.trigger: losslessness check flags entity recall < 0.90 on new chunk type batch
edge_cases.recommended_action: develop specialized distillation prompt for new chunk type; add to schema; re-run fidelity check

edge_cases.title: benchmark_contamination_detected_post_reporting
edge_cases.description: Benchmark contamination found in training corpus after benchmark results have been reported externally.
edge_cases.trigger: contamination scanner detects n-gram overlap > 5% between training data and reported benchmark
edge_cases.recommended_action: retract or caveat reported numbers; re-evaluate on clean held-out benchmark; investigate data pipeline

edge_cases.title: specialist_scope_drift_in_production
edge_cases.description: Production query distribution drifts into specialist boundary zone causing degraded accuracy without triggering out-of-scope detector.
edge_cases.trigger: production accuracy drops > 5 points while router confidence stays above threshold
edge_cases.recommended_action: retrain out-of-scope detector on recent production queries; update scope boundary definition

edge_cases.title: teacher_model_update_invalidates_cached_labels
edge_cases.description: Teacher model checkpoint updated (e.g., safety patch) causing cached soft labels to be stale and inconsistent with current teacher.
edge_cases.trigger: teacher model hash in provenance record does not match current deployed teacher hash
edge_cases.recommended_action: flag all affected records for re-distillation; do not mix label generations in training

edge_cases.title: schema_versioning_gap_breaks_renderer
edge_cases.description: Schema field renamed without version bump causes renderer to silently drop renamed field content from human-readable output.
edge_cases.trigger: rendered output missing expected content that exists in raw JSON
edge_cases.recommended_action: enforce schema version bump as CI gate; renderer integration tests cover all schema versions

edge_cases.title: orchestration_latency_sla_breach_under_load
edge_cases.description: Under high QPS load, routing + specialist inference chain exceeds SLA p95 latency budget due to queuing not modeled in cost model.
edge_cases.trigger: p95 latency exceeds SLA threshold on load test at target QPS
edge_cases.recommended_action: add queuing latency to cost model; parallelize specialist calls; add caching layer for repeated queries

edge_cases.title: human_reviewer_calibration_drift
edge_cases.description: Reviewer inter-annotator agreement drops below 0.80 over time as reviewers diverge in acceptance criteria interpretation.
edge_cases.trigger: IAA kappa drops below 0.75 on monthly calibration check
edge_cases.recommended_action: mandatory recalibration session; update review criteria checklist; resolve ambiguous cases as canonical examples

edge_cases.title: compression_ratio_target_forces_lossiness
edge_cases.description: Aggressive compression ratio target forces distillation prompt to drop low-frequency but high-value facts to meet token budget.
edge_cases.trigger: numeric fact preservation rate drops below 0.99 while compression ratio target is met
edge_cases.recommended_action: relax compression ratio target; identify which fact types are being dropped; add explicit retention instructions to prompt

edge_cases.title: cot_distillation_imports_teacher_hallucinations
edge_cases.description: Teacher CoT traces contain confident-sounding hallucinated reasoning steps that are distilled into student as ground truth.
edge_cases.trigger: student produces structurally correct reasoning but factually wrong answers on held-out factual QA
edge_cases.recommended_action: add NLI-based factual consistency check on CoT traces before training; human review high-confidence wrong traces

edge_cases.title: gpu_budget_overrun_triggers_scope_reduction
edge_cases.description: Teacher inference cost overruns GPU budget mid-project forcing reduction in corpus size or switch to smaller teacher.
edge_cases.trigger: actual GPU spend reaches 80% of budget before label generation is 50% complete
edge_cases.recommended_action: activate budget alert early; pre-approved fallback plan: switch to smaller open-weight teacher; prioritize highest-value corpus segments

workflow.gate: license compliance confirmed before any inference run
FSM compiles in < 30s; parse failure rate = 0% on 100-sample test
label cache versioned by teacher hash; deduplication confirmed; cost within budget
entity recall >= 0.95; numeric fact preservation >= 0.99; compression >= 3:1
IAA >= 0.80; high-risk record review rate >= 20%; all records have provenance fields
student latency projection meets SLA; soft-target loss ablation completed
validation loss converged; checkpoint selected by val loss not train loss
contamination scan clean; human eval correlation >= 0.75; student within 5% of teacher on target task
specialist outperforms generalist >= 10pts in scope; p95 latency within SLA on load test
all schema fields appear in rendered output; rendering roundtrip recovers >= 90% of fields
scope drift alert fires within 48h of distribution shift; fallback rate < 15%

dominance_rules.condition: teacher model ToS prohibits use of API outputs for training competing models
dominance_rules.action: select best available open-weight teacher regardless of capability gap; document capability delta
dominance_rules.rationale: legal and contractual risk of ToS violation outweighs accuracy benefit of frontier API teacher

dominance_rules.condition: entity recall < 0.95 or numeric fact preservation < 0.99 at target compression ratio
dominance_rules.action: relax compression ratio until losslessness floor is met; never sacrifice losslessness for density
dominance_rules.rationale: lossy distillation defeats the purpose of the KB and corrupts downstream use

dominance_rules.condition: constrained decoding produces any parse failure on schema-valid inputs
dominance_rules.action: halt pipeline; diagnose FSM compilation or tokenizer mismatch before continuing
dominance_rules.rationale: any parse failure propagates corrupt records silently through downstream pipeline

dominance_rules.condition: benchmark score and human eval score diverge by > 8 percentage points
dominance_rules.action: do not report benchmark score as evidence of user utility; investigate contamination or Goodhart failure
dominance_rules.rationale: Goodhart's Law means metric optimization without real-utility correlation is misleading

dominance_rules.condition: training corpus updated or new benchmark added
dominance_rules.action: run contamination scanner on training corpus against benchmark before reporting any number
dominance_rules.rationale: contaminated benchmarks inflate student scores and mislead product decisions

dominance_rules.action: scope boundary doc and out-of-scope detector must be complete and tested before routing goes live
dominance_rules.rationale: routing without scope boundary silently degrades accuracy on out-of-scope traffic

dominance_rules.condition: field renamed, removed, or type changed in JSON schema
dominance_rules.action: increment schema version; write migration script; update renderer and consumers before deploying
dominance_rules.rationale: silent schema breaks corrupt existing records and renderer output without detectable error

dominance_rules.condition: teacher inference run estimated to exceed 1k GPU-hours or 20% of total project budget
dominance_rules.action: require approved cost estimate and budget confirmation before starting run
dominance_rules.rationale: GPU cost overruns can kill projects mid-distillation leaving incomplete label caches

dominance_rules.condition: CoT trace distillation selected as primary distillation method
dominance_rules.action: human review of >= 50 sampled traces for factual correctness before any training run
dominance_rules.rationale: hallucinated CoT traces trained as ground truth corrupt student reasoning irreversibly

dominance_rules.condition: any distilled record lacks teacher_model_hash or prompt_template_hash
dominance_rules.action: block record from entering training dataset; re-distill with provenance logging enabled
dominance_rules.rationale: missing provenance makes targeted re-distillation impossible after teacher or prompt update

anti_rework_rules.rationale: schema errors discovered after 1M records are distilled require full re-distillation; fix schema first
unversioned label caches cannot be selectively invalidated; full re-cache required on teacher update
architecture change post-training requires full re-training; confirm SLA before selection
tuning on full training set causes overfit requiring re-collection of training data to correct
contaminated result requires retracting public numbers and re-evaluation on clean benchmark; run scan first
routing without tested scope boundary requires emergency rollback on first out-of-scope production failure
breaking schema change without migration corrupts all existing records requiring full re-distillation
mixed-version soft labels produce inconsistent training signal requiring full re-caching to fix
discovering systematic lossiness after distilling 500k chunks of a new type requires full re-distillation
hallucinated traces baked into training data corrupt student reasoning and require full re-training to fix

iteration_protocol.action: develop specialized distillation prompt for chunk type; re-run fidelity check; update schema if needed
iteration_protocol.exit_condition: entity recall >= 0.95 and numeric fact preservation >= 0.99 on new chunk type

iteration_protocol.action: refactor schema to remove recursion; simplify nested objects; retry compilation
iteration_protocol.exit_condition: FSM compiles in < 30s and parse failure rate = 0%

iteration_protocol.action: identify affected records via provenance graph; re-distill only affected records; update provenance
iteration_protocol.exit_condition: all records in training dataset share same teacher_model_hash

iteration_protocol.action: run contamination scan; switch to canary benchmark; investigate Goodhart failure mode
iteration_protocol.exit_condition: human eval correlation >= 0.75 and contamination scan clean

iteration_protocol.action: review scope definition; narrow task scope or increase student capacity; re-distill with narrower corpus
iteration_protocol.exit_condition: specialist outperforms generalist by >= 10 points on benchmark within defined scope

iteration_protocol.action: parallelize specialist calls; add query result caching; review routing hop count; update latency model
iteration_protocol.exit_condition: p95 latency within SLA at target QPS on load test

iteration_protocol.action: activate pre-approved fallback: switch to smaller teacher; prioritize highest-value corpus segments
iteration_protocol.exit_condition: projected total cost within approved budget with revised plan

iteration_protocol.action: increment schema version; write migration script; test on production record sample; update renderer
iteration_protocol.exit_condition: migration script tested on 1000 records; renderer updated; compatibility matrix updated

iteration_protocol.action: mandatory recalibration session; update review criteria with canonical borderline examples

priority_rationale: Foundations (KD_THEORY, TEACHER_SELECTION) gate all downstream work; schema and constrained decoding gate distillation correctness; losslessness and data pipeline gate training quality; benchmark and Goodhart gate deployment; routing and latency gate production SLA; cost, provenance, and human review gate governance and repeatability.
